description: Compare each channel's average fee rate to the simple mean of all channel averages.

b.request: Using the unweighted mean of per-channel average feerates, filter to channels whose average exceeds it, and return one unrounded row with those channels' mean average feerate and their average excess over the overall mean
b.sql: WITH chan AS (SELECT o.exchspot AS channel, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.exchspot), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS mean_rate FROM chan) SELECT AVG(c.avg_rate) AS mean_avg_feerate, AVG(c.avg_rate - o.mean_rate) AS avg_excess FROM chan c CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE c.avg_rate > o.mean_rate;

a.request: Looking at fees linked to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), compute each order channel's (`orders.orderbase`) average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values), and use the simple mean of those channel averages as the benchmark. For the channels whose average is strictly above that benchmark, return a single row with the mean of their average fee rates and the mean of how far each one exceeds the benchmark, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH channel_avg AS (SELECT o.orderbase, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL AND o.orderbase IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.orderbase), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS bench FROM channel_avg) SELECT AVG(c.avg_rate) AS mean_above_channel_avg_rate, AVG(c.avg_rate - b.bench) AS mean_excess_over_benchmark FROM channel_avg c CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE c.avg_rate > b.bench;

c.request: For fees tied to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), which order channels (`orders.orderbase`) have an above-average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values)? Give me one row: those channels' mean average fee rate and, on average, how far above average they are, unrounded. Compare each channel's average fee rate to the simple mean of all channel averages.
c.sql:
WITH channel_avg AS (
  SELECT o.orderbase, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_rate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.orderbase
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS overall_mean FROM channel_avg
),
above AS (
  SELECT c.orderbase, c.avg_rate, c.avg_rate - g.overall_mean AS excess
  FROM channel_avg c
  CROSS JOIN overall g
  WHERE c.avg_rate > g.overall_mean
)
SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS mean_above_channel_avg_feerate,
       AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_above_mean
FROM above;

d.request: Compare each order channel's average fee rate (for fees linked to orders, ignoring missing feerate values) to the simple mean of all channel averages.
d.sql: WITH channel_avg AS (SELECT o.exchspot AS channel, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.exchspot) SELECT channel, avg_feerate, AVG(avg_feerate) OVER () AS mean_of_channel_avgs, avg_feerate - AVG(avg_feerate) OVER () AS diff_from_mean FROM channel_avg ORDER BY channel;
